body.title: fix: render the inline-config Secret as `data` so removed sections are pruned
body.body:
Fixes #1109

The inline-config Secret used `stringData`. The API server stores it as `data`, so a section removed from `gitea.config` was never pruned from the live Secret, and the init container kept writing it into `app.ini` on every start. With Gitea 28, a leftover `[webhook] ALLOWED_HOST_LIST` overrides `[security]`'s, which breaks webhooks to private hosts.

This renders the Secret as base64 `data` instead.

- `templates/secret_inlineConfig.yaml`: `stringData` → `data` (`b64enc`).
- Unit tests read `data.*` with `decodeBase64: true`; adds a regression test asserting there is no `stringData`.

Note: keys that are already stale from the `stringData` era survive the first upgrade to this version, because Helm's three-way merge never recorded them under `data`. Every removal after that is pruned.

`make unittests-helm`: 261 passed. `helm lint` and `yamllint` are clean.

body.title: Removing a section from gitea.config leaves it in the inline-config Secret (and app.ini)
body.body:
Removing a section from `gitea.config` doesn't remove it from the running instance.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Install with a section, e.g.
   ```yaml
   gitea:
     config:
       webhook:
         ALLOWED_HOST_LIST: "*"
   ```
2. Remove the `webhook` section and `helm upgrade`.
3. `kubectl get secret <release>-inline-config -o jsonpath='{.data.webhook}' | base64 -d` still prints `ALLOWED_HOST_LIST=*`, and the init container writes it into `app.ini` again on every start.

**Cause**

`templates/secret_inlineConfig.yaml` uses `stringData`. The API server merges `stringData` into `data` and stores only `data`. On upgrade, Helm's patch removes the key from `stringData`, which doesn't affect the stored `data`, so the stale key stays in the Secret indefinitely.

**Impact**

This shows up with Gitea 28. A leftover `[webhook] ALLOWED_HOST_LIST` overrides `[security] ALLOWED_HOST_LIST`, and the old `*` value is now rejected as invalid. That leaves the list empty, so every webhook to a private address fails with `denied by egress policy ... needs an explicit allow entry`, even after the user has migrated their values as documented.

**Proposed fix**

Render the Secret as base64 `data`, so removed keys are pruned on upgrade.
